questions.question: What was special about the bush Moses saw at Horeb?
options: It was glowing brightly but not hot to the touch.
It was burning with fire but not being consumed.
It was speaking in a human voice without any fire.
It was surrounded by a bright light, but the bush itself was normal.
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says, 'behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.'

questions.question: What did Moses say when God first called his name from the bush?
options: "Who are you?"
"I am here."
"Here am I."
"What do you want?"
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states, 'God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I.'

questions.question: Why did God tell Moses to take off his shoes?
options: As a sign of humility before God.
To prepare for a long journey through the desert.
Because the ground he was standing on was holy.
So he could feel the earth beneath his feet.
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says, 'put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.'

questions.question: What does the phrase 'a land flowing with milk and honey' mean in this passage?
options: A land where there are many cows and bees.
A land that is very fertile and full of good things.
A land where people drink milk and eat honey every day.
A land that is sweet and easy to live in without any work.
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 17 describe the land God will bring the Israelites to as 'a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey,' implying it is rich and abundant, contrasted with their 'affliction in Egypt.'

questions.question: When Moses asked God what His name was, what specific name did God tell him to use for the children of Israel?
options: The Lord God of your fathers.
I Am That I Am.
The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
The God who will deliver them.
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says, 'And God said unto Moses, I Am That I Am: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I Am hath sent me unto you.'
